summary: Marina del Rey packs nearly 9,000 residents into just 1.5 square miles, making it one of the densest communities on the California coast — yet almost all of that density is oriented around the largest man-made small-craft harbor in North America, so the dominant visual isn't concrete but masts, waterfront promenades, and an unobstructed western horizon that delivers Pacific sunsets at eye level. The flat, sea-level terrain and compact footprint make most errands walkable or bikeable, and the Marvin Braude Bike Trail runs right through, connecting south to Playa del Rey and north toward Venice and Santa Monica. With a median household income of $142,440 and a median home value around $470,600, the buy-in looks moderate by Westside Los Angeles standards — until you notice median rent sits at $3,501 a month, reflecting that much of the housing stock is rental apartments and condominiums rather than single-family homes. The 0.8% poverty rate and 76.7% bachelor's-degree attainment rate signal a workforce heavily tied to the entertainment, tech, and professional-services firms clustered along Silicon Beach. Annual highs averaging 71°F with 9.2 hours of daily sunshine means the mild, marine-layer-moderated climate barely has seasons. The essential tension: you get waterfront living at urban density, but in a place so small that your neighborhood *is* the entire city.
